questions.question: If the largest angle in a triangle is 75°, what is the least possible value of the smallest angle of the triangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a triangle, to **minimize the smallest angle**, the other two angles must be as large as possible.

Given the **largest angle** is 75°, the second-largest angle can at most be 75°.

Least possible smallest angle = 180° − (Largest Angle + Max possible second angle)

Least possible smallest angle = 180° − (75° + 75°) = 180° − 150° = 30°.

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The **largest angle** of the triangle is 75°.

**Formula Used:** The sum of all **interior angles** of a triangle is always 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4b952771d4807331d3323e6d8c82d892cb36aba9792cbc38dee12ea4207c5974.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the three angles of the triangle be x, y, and z.

⇒ According to the question, let the **largest angle** z = 75°.

⇒ By the **Angle Sum Property**: x + y + z = 180°

⇒ x + y + 75° = 180°

⇒ x + y = 180° − 75° = 105°

⇒ To find the **least possible value** of the smallest angle (x), we must **maximize** the second angle (y).

⇒ Since 75° is the **maximum angle**, y cannot exceed 75°. So, the **maximum value** of y = 75°.

⇒ Least value of x = 105° − 75° = 30°.

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle Sum Property

The sum of the three interior angles of any Euclidean triangle is always 180°.

Types of Triangles by Angles

Acute (all angles 90°).

Isosceles Triangle Property

In this problem, the minimum value occurs when the triangle is **isosceles** with two angles equal to 75°.</p

questions.question: The axis of the earth is inclined to the plane of ecliptic at an angle of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**66(1)/(2)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The axis of the Earth is inclined at an angle of **66(1)/(2) degrees** to the plane of the ecliptic.
 
• This inclination is responsible for the **changing seasons** on Earth.
 
• Because of this tilt, different parts of the Earth receive varying amounts of sunlight throughout the year.
 
• The tilt remains relatively constant over time, although it can undergo minor variations due to gravitational interactions with other celestial bodies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Axis of the Earth**

 
 
• The Earth rotates around an imaginary line called the axis, which passes through the North and South Poles.
 
• The axis is tilted at an angle of approximately 23.5 degrees relative to the orbital plane of the Earth around the Sun.
 
• This tilt is what causes the variation in the amount of sunlight different parts of the Earth receive, leading to the phenomenon of seasons.
 
 
 
• **Plane of the Ecliptic**
 
 
• The plane of the ecliptic is the imaginary plane that contains the Earth's orbit around the Sun.
 
• It is used as a reference plane for the solar system, and most of the planets in the solar system orbit within a few degrees of this plane.
 
• The apparent path that the Sun traces out in the sky over the course of a year, as observed from Earth, is also called the ecliptic.
 
 
 
• **Seasons**
 
 
• The tilt of the Earth's axis and its orbit around the Sun cause the seasons.
 
• When the Northern Hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun, it experiences summer while the Southern Hemisphere experiences winter, and vice versa.
 
• During spring and autumn (fall), both hemispheres receive approximately equal amounts of sunlight.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Interactions**
 
 
• The Earth's tilt can undergo minor changes due to gravitational interactions with the Moon and other planets.
 
• These interactions can cause the axis to wobble slightly in a phenomenon known as axial precession.
 
• Axial precession is a slow, continuous change in the orientation of the Earth's rotational axis, which can affect long-term climate patterns.

questions.question: Through which of the following cities does Hudson River flow?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New York**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Hudson River flows through the state of New York in the United States.
 
• It originates from the Adirondack Mountains and flows southward through the Hudson Valley to New York City.
 
• The river is named after the English explorer Henry Hudson, who navigated it in 1609.
 
• The Hudson River is approximately 315 miles (507 kilometers) long.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Henry Hudson:**

 
 
• Henry Hudson was an English sea explorer and navigator during the early 17th century.
 
• He is best known for his explorations of present-day Canada and parts of the northeastern United States.
 
• The Hudson River, Hudson Strait, and Hudson Bay are named after him.
 
 
 
• **Adirondack Mountains:**
 
 
• The Adirondack Mountains are a mountain range located in the northeastern part of New York State.
 
• They are part of the larger Appalachian Mountains and cover approximately 5,000 square miles.
 
• The region is known for its beautiful landscapes, extensive forests, and numerous lakes and rivers.
 
 
 
• **Hudson Valley:**
 
 
• The Hudson Valley is a region in New York State that stretches along the Hudson River from the Capital District in the north to the New York City metropolitan area in the south.
 
• It is known for its natural beauty, historic sites, and vibrant cultural scene.
 
• The valley has been an important area for agriculture, industry, and transportation throughout the history of New York State.

questions.question: Vikram Samvat calendar is ______ years ahead of the Gregorian calendar.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**56.7**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Vikram Samvat calendar is a historical Hindu calendar used in India and Nepal.
 
• It is approximately 56.7 years ahead of the Gregorian calendar, which is the calendar used by most of the world today.
 
• The Vikram Samvat calendar was started in 57 BCE by the Indian king Vikramaditya.
 
• This calendar is a lunisolar calendar, meaning it is based on both the phases of the moon and the solar year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vikram Samvat Calendar**

 
 
• The Vikram Samvat calendar is one of the oldest calendars still in use today and is widely used in Indian and Nepalese culture for religious festivals and traditional events.
 
• It is a lunisolar calendar, which means it takes into account both the moon phases and the solar year, similar to the Hebrew and Chinese calendars.
 
• Each month in the Vikram Samvat calendar is divided into two parts: the bright half (Shukla Paksha) and the dark half (Krishna Paksha), based on the waxing and waning phases of the moon.
 
• The new year in the Vikram Samvat calendar typically starts in mid-April, coinciding with the Hindu festival of Baisakhi.
 
 
 
• **Gregorian Calendar**
 
 
• The Gregorian calendar is the calendar that is most commonly used today worldwide. It was introduced by Pope Gregory XIII in 1582.
 
• This calendar is a solar calendar, based solely on the Earth's revolutions around the Sun.
 
• It replaced the Julian calendar, which was less accurate in terms of aligning with the solar year.
 
• The Gregorian calendar is organized into 12 months, with a leap year occurring every four years to account for the extra 0.25 days in each year.

What is the real name of Babur?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zahir-ud-din**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Zahir-ud-din Muhammad Babur** was the founder and first Emperor of the Mughal dynasty in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Babur was born on **14 February 1483** in the city of Andijan, in present-day Uzbekistan.
 
• Babur was a descendant of **Timur on his father's side** and **Genghis Khan on his mother's side**.
 
• He established the Mughal Empire in 1526 after his victory at the **First Battle of Panipat** against Ibrahim Lodi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Babur's Early Life**

 
 
• Babur was born in the Fergana Valley, which is now part of Uzbekistan.
 
• He became a ruler at the young age of 12 after the death of his father, Umar Sheikh Mirza.
 
• Initially, he faced numerous challenges including opposition from his uncles and other regional rulers.
 
• Despite several early setbacks, Babur managed to capture and consolidate territories over time.
 
 
 
• **Timurid Dynasty**
 
 
• The Timurid dynasty was founded by Timur (also known as Tamerlane), a Turco-Mongol conqueror who established a vast empire in Central Asia.
 
• Babur, being a Timurid prince, inherited a claim to the thrones of both Ferghana and Samarkand.
 
• The Timurids were known for their patronage of arts and architecture, which greatly influenced Babur's tastes and policies.
 
 
 
• **Genghis Khan's Legacy**
 
 
• Babur's maternal lineage traced back to Genghis Khan, the founder of the Mongol Empire.
 
• This gave Babur a prestigious heritage, combining the legacies of two of the most powerful conquerors in history.
 
• Genghis Khan's descendants, known as the Chagatai Khanate, ruled over parts of Central Asia, which had a significant impact on Babur's early life and ambitions.
 
 
 
• **First Battle of Panipat**
 
 
• Fought on 21 April 1526 between Babur and the Sultan of Delhi, Ibrahim Lodi.
 
• The battle marked the beginning of Mughal rule in India.
 
• Babur's use of field artillery and innovative tactics played a crucial role in his victory.
 
• This battle is often cited as one of the earliest instances of modern military strategy in the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: Where is the headquarters of International Committee of the Red Cross situated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Geneva**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) is headquartered in **Geneva, Switzerland**.
 
• ICRC was founded in 1863 and is one of the most respected humanitarian organizations globally.
 
• The ICRC plays a unique role in international humanitarian law and the protection of victims of armed conflict.
 
• It operates worldwide, assisting people affected by conflict and armed violence and promoting the laws that protect victims of war.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)**

 
 
• The ICRC is an independent, neutral organization ensuring humanitarian protection and assistance for victims of armed conflict and other situations of violence.
 
• It is part of the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement along with the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) and 192 National Societies.
 
• The ICRC's mandate stems from the Geneva Conventions of 1949, which are international treaties that contain the most important rules limiting the barbarity of war.
 
• The ICRC works to protect and assist victims of armed conflict and strives to ensure respect for international humanitarian law.
 
 
 
• **Geneva Conventions**
 
 
• The Geneva Conventions are four treaties formulated in Geneva, Switzerland, that set the standards in international law for humanitarian treatment in war.
 
• The Conventions were first adopted in 1864 and were significantly updated in 1949 after World War II.
 
• They are universally ratified and form the core of international humanitarian law.
 
• The conventions protect those who are not participating in hostilities, such as civilians, health workers, and aid workers, as well as those who are no longer participating, like wounded soldiers and prisoners of war.
 
 
 
• **International Humanitarian Law (IHL)**
 
 
• Also known as the laws of war or the law of armed conflict, IHL is a set of rules which seek, for humanitarian reasons, to limit the effects of armed conflict.
 
• IHL protects persons who are not or are no longer participating in the hostilities and restricts the means and methods of warfare.
 
• The core instruments of IHL are the Geneva Conventions and their Additional Protocols.
 
• IHL is part of international law, which is the body of rules governing relations between states.

questions.question: The Jim Corbett National Park was established in 1936 to save the endangered species of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bengal tiger**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Jim Corbett National Park was established in 1936 as Hailey National Park to protect the endangered Bengal tiger.
 
• It was renamed in 1956 after the famous hunter and conservationist Jim Corbett who played a key role in its establishment.
 
• It is located in the Nainital district of Uttarakhand, India.
 
• The park is known for its rich biodiversity and is a major attraction for wildlife enthusiasts and nature lovers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bengal Tiger (Panthera tigris tigris)**

 
 
• The Bengal tiger is a tiger population native to the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It is the most numerous tiger subspecies, and it is listed as Endangered on the IUCN Red List.
 
• The Bengal tiger's coat is yellow to light orange, with stripes ranging from dark brown to black.
 
• It is a top predator and an apex predator in its ecosystem, playing a crucial role in maintaining the balance of the ecosystem by controlling the population of herbivores and other animals.
 
 
 
• **Jim Corbett (1875-1955)**
 
 
• Jim Corbett was a British-Indian hunter, tracker, naturalist, and author who hunted a number of man-eating tigers and leopards in India.
 
• He authored several books recounting his hunts and experiences, the most famous being "Man-Eaters of Kumaon".
 
• Corbett was an early advocate of wildlife conservation in India and played a key role in the establishment of wildlife sanctuaries.
 
• In recognition of his efforts, the Hailey National Park was renamed Jim Corbett National Park.
 
 
 
• **National Parks in India**
 
 
• National parks are protected areas, established by the government to conserve wildlife and natural habitats.
 
• India has over 100 national parks, each playing a vital role in the conservation of biodiversity.
 
• These parks provide a sanctuary for various endangered species and are important for scientific research and education.
 
• National parks also promote eco-tourism and provide opportunities for people to experience and appreciate nature.
 
 
 
• **Wildlife Conservation**
 
 
• Wildlife conservation involves the protection and management of wildlife species and their habitats to prevent extinction.
 
• Efforts include establishing protected areas, anti-poaching measures, habitat restoration, and breeding programs.
 
• Conservation is crucial for maintaining biodiversity, which is essential for ecosystem stability and human well-being.
 
• International cooperation and policies like the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) play a significant role in global wildlife conservation efforts.

questions.question: ₹4,800 becomes ₹6,000 in 4 years at a certain rate of compound interest. What will be the amount after 12 years at the same rate of compound interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹4,800

Amount after 4 years (A₁) = ₹6,000

Time (t) = 4 years

**Formula used:**

A = P × [1 + (r/100)]t

Where, A = Amount, P = Principal, r = rate of interest, t = time (in years)

**Calculations:**

We are given that the amount after 4 years is ₹6,000, so we can write the equation:

6000 = 4800 × [1 + (r/100)]⁴ ----(1)

Now, let's calculate the amount after 12 years using the same formula:

A = 4800 × [1 + (r/100)]¹² ----(2)

First, we need to find the rate of interest. To do this, we divide equation (2) by equation (1):

⇒ (A₂ / A₁) = [1 + (r/100)]¹² / [1 + (r/100)]⁴

⇒ (A₂ / A₁) = [1 + (r/100)]⁸

Substitute the values of A₂ and A₁:

⇒ (A₂ / 6000) = [1 + (r/100)]⁸

Substitute the known values from equation (1):

⇒ (6000 / 4800) = [1 + (r/100)]⁴

⇒ 5/4 = [1 + (r/100)]⁴

⇒ (5/4)¹/⁴ = 1 + (r/100)

⇒ (1.25)¹/⁴ = 1 + (r/100)

⇒ 1.0574 ≈ 1 + (r/100)

⇒ r/100 = 1.0574 - 1

⇒ r/100 = 0.0574

⇒ r ≈ 5.74%

**Now that we have the rate of interest, we can calculate the amount after 12 years (A₂):**

Substitute r = 5.74% in equation (2):

A = 4800 × [1 + (5.74/100)]¹²

A = 4800 × (1.0574)¹²

A ≈ 4800 × 1.9508

A ≈ ₹9,375

**The amount after 12 years will be ₹9,375.**

questions.question: Bengal Gazette, the first major newspaper in India, started in the year ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1780**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bengal Gazette** was the first major newspaper in India, marking the beginning of print journalism in the country.
 
• The paper was started by **James Augustus Hicky**, who is often referred to as the "father of Indian press".
 
• The first issue of Bengal Gazette was published on **29 January 1780**.
 
• The newspaper was also known as **Hicky's Gazette** and was characterized by its open criticism of the British Government in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **James Augustus Hicky:**

 
 
• James Augustus Hicky was an Irishman who launched the Bengal Gazette, the first English-language newspaper in India.
 
• He used the newspaper as a platform to criticize the policies and actions of the British East India Company and its officials.
 
• His outspoken nature and investigative journalism led to multiple legal issues with the British authorities.
 
• Despite his efforts to bring transparency, the newspaper was shut down by the British government in 1782.
 
 
 
• **History of Indian Journalism:**
 
 
• The Bengal Gazette paved the way for other publications in India, with newspapers becoming a significant medium for information and public discourse.
 
• In the early 19th century, several newspapers emerged, such as The Calcutta Journal, The Bombay Herald, and The Madras Courier.
 
• These publications played a crucial role in the Indian independence movement by spreading nationalist ideas and mobilizing public opinion against colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Print Media Evolution:**
 
 
• The evolution of print media in India saw a transition from colonial-controlled press to a more diversified and free press post-independence.
 
• Post-independence, newspapers like The Times of India, The Hindu, and Indian Express became prominent in shaping public opinion and providing news coverage.
 
• Today, India's print media landscape includes a multitude of newspapers in various languages, catering to diverse audiences across the country.

questions.question: Which of the following countries has the highest male to female population ratio in the world in 2019?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Qatar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Qatar has the highest male to female population ratio in the world, with significantly more males than females.
 
• This skewed ratio is primarily due to the high number of male expatriates in the country, many of whom are laborers working in various sectors like construction.
 
• The influx of male workers is driven by Qatar's rapid economic development and infrastructural projects, especially those related to the FIFA World Cup 2022 preparations.
 
• The male to female ratio in Qatar is approximately 3.1:1, meaning there are around three males for every female in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Male to Female Population Ratio**

 
 
• This ratio indicates the number of males for every female in a population.
 
• A ratio of 1:1 indicates an equal number of males and females.
 
• Countries with large numbers of male labor migrants often have higher ratios of males to females.
 
 
 
• **Expatriates**
 
 
• Expatriates, or expats, are people who reside in a country other than their native country.
 
• In countries like Qatar, a significant portion of the workforce consists of expatriates.
 
• The majority of expatriates in Qatar are males who have migrated for work opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Labor Migration**
 
 
• Labor migration refers to the movement of people from one country to another for the purpose of employment.
 
• Countries with booming economies and large-scale infrastructure projects attract labor migrants.

questions.solution:
**Given:**

A group of men decided to complete a task in 10 days, but five of them remained absent. If the rest of the group completed the task in 12 days, find the original number of men in the group.

**Formula used:**

Work = Number of men × Number of days

**Calculation:**

Let the original number of men be x .

Work = x men × 10 days

When 5 men are absent, the remaining men are x - 5 .

Work = (x - 5) men × 12 days

Since the amount of work is the same:

x times 10 = (x - 5) times 12

⇒ 10x = 12(x - 5)

⇒ 10x = 12x - 60

⇒ 60 = 2x

⇒ x = 30

**∴ The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: A person travelled 120 km by steamer, 450 km by train and 60 km by horse. It took 13 h 30 min. If the speed of the train is 3 times that of the horse and 1.5 times that of the steamer, find the speed of the train.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A person travelled 120 km by steamer, 450 km by train and 60 km by horse.

It took 13 h 30 min.

The speed of the train is 3 times that of the horse and 1.5 times that of the steamer.

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of the horse be x km/h.

Therefore, speed of the train = 3x km/h

Speed of the steamer = 3x / 1.5 = 2x km/h

Total time taken = 13.5 hours

Time taken by steamer = 120 / 2x hours

Time taken by train = 450 / 3x hours

Time taken by horse = 60 / x hours

Total time taken = (120 / 2x) + (450 / 3x) + (60 / x)

⇒ 13.5 = (120 / 2x) + (450 / 3x) + (60 / x)

⇒ 13.5 = 60 / x + 150 / x + 60 / x

⇒ 13.5 = (60 + 150 + 60) / x

⇒ 13.5 = 270 / x

⇒ x = 270 / 13.5

⇒ x = 20 km/h

Speed of the train = 3x = 3 × 20 = 60 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: The total number of gold medals and silver medals won by a person in games is 75. Which of the following CANNOT be the ratio of number of silver medals won by that person?

⇒ 5x = 75

Ratio 2:3 is possible.

⇒ 9x + 1x = 75

⇒ 10x = 75

⇒ x = 7.5

⇒ S = 9×7.5 = 67.5, G = 1×7.5 = 7.5

Since the number of medals cannot be in fractions, ratio 9:1 is not possible.

⇒ 12x + 13x = 75

⇒ 25x = 75

⇒ x = 3

⇒ S = 12×3 = 36, G = 13×3 = 39

• **Locks:**

questions.question: According to the law of diminishing marginal utility, as the amount of a good consumed increases, the marginal utility of that good tends to ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**diminish**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the law of diminishing marginal utility, the additional satisfaction (utility) gained from consuming additional units of a good decreases as more of the good is consumed.
 
• This principle is fundamental in understanding consumer choice and behavior in economics.
 
• The law of diminishing marginal utility implies that each subsequent unit of a good consumed adds less to total utility than the previous unit.
 
• This concept helps explain why demand curves typically slope downward, as consumers are willing to buy more of a good only at lower prices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marginal Utility (MU):**

 
 
• Marginal utility is the additional satisfaction or benefit (utility) that a consumer derives from consuming an additional unit of a good or service.
 
• It is calculated as the change in total utility divided by the change in the quantity of the good consumed.
 
 
 
• **Total Utility (TU):**
 
 
• Total utility is the overall satisfaction or benefit that a consumer receives from consuming a certain quantity of goods or services.
 
• It is the sum of the marginal utilities of all units consumed.
 
 
 
• **Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility:**
 
 
• This law states that as a person consumes more units of a good, the additional satisfaction (marginal utility) from each additional unit decreases.
 
• For example, the first slice of pizza may provide a lot of satisfaction, but by the fourth or fifth slice, the additional satisfaction gained decreases.
 
 
 
• **Implications for Consumer Behavior:**
 
 
• The law of diminishing marginal utility explains why consumers are willing to pay less for additional units of a good.
 
• It is a key reason behind the downward-sloping demand curve in economics.

4 players join the team, increasing the average age by 2 years.

**Calculation:**

Sum of age of 11 players = 11 × 18 = 198

Since 4 players join the team, increasing the average age by 2 years.

Total players = 11 + 4 = 15

New average = 18 + 2 = 20

So, Sum of age of all players = 15 × 20 = 300

Now,

Sum of age of 4 players = 300 - 198 = 102

So, average of age of 4 players = 102/4 = 25.5 years

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**
